clue.text: Youngsters boxing on ship — or training for it?

indicators.note: the youngsters are boxing in the sense of enclosing what follows, holding it inside them

parts.note: pups are young animals, here youngsters
re means on or concerning
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Young boxers fighting aboard a ship, with a wry question about how they prepare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to boxing: the floor exercise is part of a boxer's training, so the definition rides on the surface's own word.
explanation.definitionFit: Push-up style floor exercises are a staple of a boxer's fitness regime, so they are training for that sport.

clue.text: Factories left rubbish outside

indicators.note: the rubbish word sits outside, wrapped round the letter for left

parts.note: pants is British slang for rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: Factories have abandoned their garbage outside the premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' as slang for rubbish is everyday British usage: 'that film was pants'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant is an industrial works, so plants is a synonym for factories.

clue.text: Written another way, 8 — 2s = 7

indicators.note: writing the letters another way means rearranging them into a different order

parts.note: the clue refers to the solution of 8 down, used here as letters
two S letters, the ones taken away by the minus sign

explanation.surface: A mock equation: rewrite one entry, subtract two esses, and you reach another entry.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash acts as a minus sign: take two S's from the 8-down answer and rearrange the remaining ENDUER. The equals sign leads to the definition, 7, the answer to 7 down, meaning tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: The 7-down answer means tolerate or put up with, which is a synonym of bear or suffer something patiently.

clue.text: Assault witnessed in Sunday School

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Someone saw an attack take place at a church Sunday School.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sunday School' reads as one thing but splits into S and the school ETON, a famous English private school near Windsor; 'witnessed in' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: To set on someone is to attack them, a phrasal verb synonymous with assault.

clue.text: In Cologne, force agent to lift essential documents

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting raises the letters so they read from the bottom up

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent
F is the physics abbreviation for force

indicators.note: essential means at the core, so the central letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: In a German city, a police force pressures an agent to steal key papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cologne' looks like the German city in the surface, but it is eau de cologne, the scent.
explanation.definitionFit: Cologne is a light scented water, a kind of fragrance, so it is defined by the broader word for scent.

clue.text: One might be agile, diving around and letting nothing in

definitions.text: One might be agile, diving around and letting nothing in

indicators.note: letting something in places it inside the rearranged letters
completes the instruction to put the letter inside
diving about suggests the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: O is the round figure for zero or nothing

explanation.surface: A description of a nimble keeper flinging themselves about and conceding no goals.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the description: AGILE rearranged around O.
explanation.definitionFit: A goalkeeper dives about the goalmouth, and success means conceding no goals at all.

clue.text: Futuristic transport heading off into the sea?

indicators.note: the heading or first letter is taken off

parts.note: a hoverboard is the floating skateboard of science fiction, as in Back to the Future

explanation.surface: A sci-fi vehicle sets off heading out over the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' reads as setting out, but it removes the first letter, H.
explanation.definitionFit: Going over the side of a vessel means falling into the water, the question mark flagging the loose phrasing.

clue.text: Tolerate ridiculous view held by drunken husband

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are held inside the word for drunk

parts.note: lit is slang for drunk

indicators.note: something ridiculous is absurd, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Putting up with the absurd opinions of an intoxicated spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' looks like it describes the husband, but it supplies LIT, slang for drunk, holding the jumbled VEWI.
explanation.definitionFit: To put up with something unwelcome is to accept and bear it, so the phrase is an idiom for tolerate.

clue.text: Rudeness irritated customers, finally

definitions.note: the final customers in a supply chain, the ones who actually use a product

indicators.note: irritated suggests stirred up, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Annoyed by rude treatment, the customers at last complained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' looks like a closing comment on the surface but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The people at the last link of a supply chain, who consume a product, are its ultimate buyers.

clue.text: Conservative leaves criminal court — day one of hearing

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order
the Conservative leaves, meaning that letter is dropped from the pool

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Tory politician walks out of a criminal court on the first day of a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal court' looks like a phrase but 'criminal' rearranges COURT, DAY and I once 'leaves' has removed C.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditory is the adjective relating to the sense of hearing or the ears.

clue.text: Intense, raging fire in which five died

indicators.note: the letter for five goes inside the rearranged letters
a raging fire is wild, so its letters are thrown about

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A violent blaze in which five people perished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raging' rearranges FIRE to FERI, and V goes into it before D.
explanation.definitionFit: Fervid means passionately ardent or burning with feeling, a synonym of intense.

clue.text: Have eight pints at a party

parts.note: a gallon is eight pints, abbreviated gal

explanation.surface: Drinking a gallon of beer at a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive celebration or social occasion, so it is a kind of party.

clue.text: Predator exists thanks to natural adaptation

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks

indicators.note: an adaptation reshapes something, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A hunter survives because of natural evolutionary change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exists' and 'to' are link words: TA then the rearranged NATURAL.
explanation.definitionFit: This large hairy spider hunts and kills insects and small animals, so it is a predator.

clue.text: Trunks, we hear, in which Jack's the centre of attention

definitions.text: in which Jack's the centre of attention
definitions.note: a game in which the small white target ball, the jack, is what players aim at

indicators.note: what we hear signals a word that sounds the same as another

parts.note: boles are tree trunks

explanation.surface: Swimming shorts, apparently, where a man named Jack draws every eye.
explanation.walkthrough: BOWLS is a lawn game, popular in Britain, where players roll balls towards a small white ball called the jack.
explanation.definitionFit: In lawn bowls every ball is rolled to finish near the jack, the small target ball.

clue.text: Ominous rainclouds beginning to appear — peg out clothes?

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here: the word for peg out dresses or wraps the letter

parts.note: to peg out is informal for to die

indicators.note: the beginning means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Threatening clouds are gathering, so should we hang out the washing?
explanation.walkthrough: 'peg out clothes' suggests laundry, but 'peg out' is DIE and 'clothes' wraps it round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Dire describes something dreadful or foreboding, a synonym of ominous.

clue.text: Cross delivered by Italian players, time and time again

parts.note: Inter is the Milan football club, Internazionale
sec is short for second, a unit of time
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A cross pass delivered by Italian footballers over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time and time again' reads as an idiom for repeatedly, but supplies two separate abbreviations for time.
explanation.definitionFit: To intersect is for lines or roads to meet and pass across each other, so it means cross.

clue.text: It's right to be in love — not entirely a requirement for successful mating?

indicators.note: the word for right goes inside the word for love
not entirely means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to adore is to love
apt means right or suitable

explanation.surface: A romantic thought that being in love is what's needed for a good match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mating' looks romantic but refers to plugs that mate: a connecting fitting lets two incompatible parts join.
explanation.definitionFit: A connector lets incompatible plugs or parts mate together, so it is what makes such a coupling work.

clue.text: Reliable car, losing hub, can be taken in

indicators.note: the hub is the middle, so the central letter of the word goes

parts.note: edible means fit to be eaten, taken in as food

explanation.surface: A dependable car missing a wheel hub can be accepted as a trade-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be taken in' suggests being fooled or trading in a car, but means fit to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Credible means believable or trustworthy, so it is close in sense to reliable.

clue.text: City girl somehow gave in

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the word for girl

parts.note: a lass is a girl

indicators.note: somehow says the letters arrive in some other order

explanation.surface: A city girl somehow surrendered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City girl' reads as one phrase, but 'City' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nevada gambling resort is a famous American city.

clue.text: Chap takes a cab — one going off duty

indicators.note: the man's name takes the letter inside it

parts.note: Rod is a man's name, a chap

indicators.note: the numeral goes off, so it is removed from the word

parts.note: a taxi is a cab
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A man hails a taxi whose driver is just finishing for the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off duty' reads as a phrase, but 'duty' is the definition and 'one going off' removes I. Road tax is the British annual vehicle excise charge.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the annual charge for using a vehicle on public roads is a tax, a kind of duty.

clue.text: Telling picture of men with guns and axes, embracing

indicators.note: the axes embrace, holding the gunners inside

parts.note: X and Y are the two axes of a graph
RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners

explanation.surface: A revealing image of armed men carrying axes, hugging each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'axes' looks like choppers but means graph axes, X and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiograph reveals what lies hidden beneath the skin, so it is an image that tells all.

clue.text: Unclear about current music technology

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: dim means faint or unclear
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone is vague about present-day music technology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like an adjective meaning modern, but it is the physics symbol I.
explanation.definitionFit: MIDI is the digital interface standard letting synthesisers and computers exchange musical data.

clue.text: Served up endless dry cheese and fortified wine

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means the letters are read upwards
endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: arid means dry
Edam is a Dutch cheese

explanation.surface: A host serves a dried-out cheese with a glass of port-style wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims ARID to ARI; ARI plus EDAM, read upwards, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a wine from the Atlantic island, strengthened with added brandy like sherry or port.

clue.text: Okay then, extremists have left town

indicators.note: the extremes, the letters at each end, have gone from the word

parts.note: Brighton is a seaside resort on England's south coast

explanation.surface: Fine, the radicals have quit the town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremists' suggests radicals but means the end letters, B and N, of BRIGHTON, a south-coast English resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Righto is informal British agreement, an interjection meaning all right or very well.

clue.text: Group captured in truck not typically problematic

indicators.note: a group of letters is held captive inside these words

explanation.surface: Gang members caught in a lorry, which is not usually so troublesome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group' looks like a gang but describes the run of letters held within the words.
explanation.definitionFit: A knotty problem is tangled and hard to solve, so knotty means difficult or troublesome.

clue.text: Port where two rivers converge

indicators.note: converging rivers run together, so the two pieces join side by side

parts.note: the phrase two rivers names a pair of rivers: the first is the Dove, which flows through Derbyshire and Staffordshire
the second river is R, the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A harbour town where two streams meet.
explanation.walkthrough: DOVER is the English Channel ferry port in Kent; 'two rivers' supplies both the River Dove, in the English Midlands, and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover is the chief English Channel ferry harbour, a famous port on the Kent coast.

clue.text: Need extra key to gain entry

indicators.note: the key letter gains entry, going inside the word

parts.note: an addition is something extra
C is a musical key

explanation.surface: You need an additional key to get in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' suggests a door key, but it is a musical key, C.
explanation.definitionFit: An addiction is a compulsive craving, a dependency that creates a constant need.

clue.text: Job centre has opening, internally

indicators.note: the first letter goes inside the word for centre

parts.note: the core is the centre

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The job centre has a vacancy within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Job centre' reads as a British employment office, but 'Job' is the definition and 'centre' gives CORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chore is a routine task, especially a tedious one, so it is a kind of job.

clue.text: Writer comes over to tour Britain, beginning in Edinburgh with iconic landmark

indicators.note: touring goes round, so the reversed word surrounds the rest
coming over means turned back to front

parts.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen
GB is Great Britain

indicators.note: the beginning is the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An author arrives for a British tour, starting in Edinburgh and visiting a famous monument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes over' turns NIB into BIN, which tours GB and E.
explanation.definitionFit: The great clock bell of the Palace of Westminster is one of London's most recognisable sights.

clue.text: Skip cold, hard bit of enchilada that's covered in cheese — no thanks!

indicators.note: the letters are covered by the cheese, which wraps round them
no thanks means the word for thanks is removed

parts.note: ricotta is an Italian soft cheese
ta is British informal for thanks
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: a bit here is the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone declines a cheesy enchilada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no thanks' sounds like a polite refusal but is a deletion instruction, leaving RICOT; 'Skip' means bounce, as a stone does.
explanation.definitionFit: To ricochet is to rebound off a surface, as a stone skips across water.

clue.text: Spielberg movie about South Africa, next to Zulu, is an inferior remake

indicators.note: the letter is placed next to the rest, after it
the film title goes about, surrounding the country

parts.note: E.T. is Steven Spielberg's 1982 film
RSA is the Republic of South Africa
Zulu is Z in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Spielberg film set in South Africa, alongside Zulu, is a poor remake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zulu' looks like the 1964 film, but it is the phonetic alphabet word for Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes an imitation or substitute that is poorer than the original.

clue.text: Grant's about to get reduced, unfortunately, for family

indicators.note: the actor's name goes about, around the other letters

parts.note: Cary Grant, the Hollywood actor

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things went wrong, so the letters are mixed up
reduced means cut short, losing the last letter

explanation.surface: Grant is about to have his payment cut, sadly for his family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant' looks like a payment but is the actor Cary Grant; 'reduced' cuts GET to GE, and with TO 'unfortunately' gives TEGO.
explanation.definitionFit: A family in classification is a grouping or class, so it is a type of class.
